sources.title: MIT 6.1400 (2025), Lecture 19: Finish NP-Completeness, coNP and Friends
sources.actual_reading: Pages 1-3: definition of NP-completeness and the theorem that SUBSET-SUM for positive integers and a positive target is NP-complete.
sources.application: Use positive-integer binary SUBSET-SUM as the source of the explicit many-one reduction in Sections 2-3 of the local note.
sources.limits: The classical Cook-Levin theorem and the complete chain of reductions are not re-proved or independently re-audited here. The new averaging reduction is given in full in the local note.

sources.title: Bertrand's Postulate, Stanford Math152A10 lecture note
sources.actual_reading: All three pages, including the prime-in-[n+1,2n] theorem and its binomial-coefficient proof.
sources.application: A prime p of size O(m), or O_alpha(m), can be found by elementary polynomial-time search over a numerical interval of that size. This bounds the number of positions and the entire reduction output length.
sources.limits: No GRH or randomized prime generation is used. The result supplies only the prime size bound, not any averaging reachability assertion.
